narrative:
I set out to kill OPP-01 and I believe I did, though not where the spec expected. The dev agent had already found and honestly disclosed the weak why-now (Rule 3-4-5 is 2023-24, not 2025-26) and had already conceded that sub-elite layering prevalence is unmeasured. Attacking those again would have been theatre. So I went at the one claim the spec never tested: that this product does not already exist on the exact order form it proposes to add it to.

It largely does. Nike Team Sports' own basketball catalogue structure lists Clothing > Bottoms as Shorts, Pants, and Tights & Capris - the four-bottom order form the spec proposes to invent is the order form Nike already publishes (niketeam.nike.com/en/en_US/nts/sport/mens/basketball, verified 2026-09-03 via search snippet; the page itself is egress-blocked from this environment). BSN Sports carries a product literally titled 'Nike Men's Pro 3/4 Length Tight' on its team catalogue (bsnsports.com/p/nike-mens-pro-34-length-tight/, same limitation). The Nike Pro HyperCool 3/4 tight is merchandised in Team Navy/Team White, Team Royal/Team White and Team Maroon/Team White - Nike's team colour naming convention, not a fitness colourway. And Nike Team Sports runs a published standing colour chart across styles (Navy, Royal, Aero Blue, Tidal Blue, Light Blue, Purple, Scarlet, Cardinal), which is exactly the 'carryover stock colour library' the spec proposes as the moat. The spec's own competitive-reference entry concedes 'the gap between this SKU and the opportunity is merchandising, colour library and channel, not capability.' Two of those three are now gone. What remains is a page layout.

The second kill is a rules error inside the spec, and it is the more interesting one. The spec makes 'dE <= 1.0 between short and tight in the same colourway' the binding engineering spec and calls it 'the entire product.' But A06-S3 - the spec's own enabling signal - says NFHS permits tights only in white, black, beige or the predominant JERSEY colour, identical across teammates. Uniform bottoms (shorts, pants, skirts) must be like-coloured to each other; tights are governed as a separate accessory class tied to the JERSEY. So the legally binding colour pairs are short-to-pant and jersey-to-tight. Short-to-tight - the pair the spec engineers, prices and defends - is not the pair the rule regulates. For the large majority of programmes the compliant tight is black, white or beige, which Nike already sells in every channel at USD 37 list and USD 26.97-32.00 street. The twelve-colour tight library the SKU matrix is built on is, for most rosters, legally unusable.

The third kill is commercial. The spec's price ceiling is Hoops King's USD 41.99 custom-sublimated tight with an 8-unit minimum, and its switching argument is 'stock beats custom on price, minimum and lead time.' But Nike's own existing stock 3/4 tight already street-prices at USD 26.97-32.00 (the spec retrieved this itself), and I found at least one custom supplier - Bear Grips, custom basketball leggings from USD 47.88 with explicitly NO minimums and free US shipping - which removes the minimum-order penalty from the custom side of the comparison. The proposed USD 30-36 team-dealer NET for a stock tight therefore sits at or above what Nike's existing stock tight already retails for. There is no price headroom in the direction the spec assumes, and the margin case was already resting entirely on an unmeasured 'low-markdown channel' claim (A04-S9 contains no basketball-shorts data of any kind).

What survives, and I want to be precise rather than dismissive: the full-length LOOSE game pant on the short's block is the one silhouette I could not confirm any major brand stocks for basketball, and the coverage/modesty need behind it is rated SUSTAINED by the auditor even though its evidence is stale (A05-S8). A knee-clearing certification across the full size grade and a 20-wash seam-and-shrinkage spec printed on a dealer sheet are real, cheap, differentiating and address the base's only reproducible consumer complaint (A01-S3, A04-S6). Those are worth doing. They are a merchandising brief and a make-quality standard on an existing catalogue - roughly one page and one test protocol - not an SS28 product opportunity. Presented as written, this loses the room to the first person who opens the Nike Team Sports site on their laptop.

One honest limit on my own attack: niketeam.nike.com, bsnsports.com, midwaysports.com, elevationsports.com, nsga.org and mhsaa.com are ALL egress-blocked from this environment. Every finding above is a converging read of search-result snippets and page titles, not a retrieved page. Four independent snippets agree, and Nike's team colour naming ('Team Navy', 'Team Royal', 'Team Maroon') is hard to produce by accident - but a PLM should spend the ten minutes to open the catalogue directly before either funding or killing this, and that check is the cheapest thing in the validation plan.

kill_attempts.angle: Is it actually NEW? Does Nike already sell this on this order form?
kill_attempts.argument: The spec's core proposition is 'four bottoms - short, 3/4 tight, full tight, full-length pant - orderable together on one roster order form in one team colour.' I attacked this by going to the order form itself. Nike Team Sports' basketball catalogue already structures Clothing > Bottoms as Shorts, Pants, and Tights & Capris. BSN Sports already lists a product titled 'Nike Men's Pro 3/4 Length Tight' in its team catalogue. The Nike Pro HyperCool 3/4 tight is already merchandised in Team Navy/Team White, Team Royal/Team White and Team Maroon/Team White - Nike's team-colour naming, not retail fitness colourways. And Nike Team Sports publishes a standing cross-style colour chart (Navy, Royal, Aero Blue, Tidal Blue, Light Blue, Purple, Scarlet, Cardinal). The spec proposes to invent the order form, the colour library and the team-colour tight. All three appear to exist.
kill_attempts.evidence: niketeam.nike.com/en/en_US/nts/sport/mens/basketball (category structure: Bottoms = Shorts, Pants, Tights & Capris), verified 2026-09-03 via search snippet - page egress-blocked. bsnsports.com/p/nike-mens-pro-34-length-tight/ and bsnsports.com/p/nike-pro-34-tight/ (product titles in team catalogue), same limitation. Nike Pro HyperCool 3/4 tight team colourways via midwaysports.com/products/1224613. Nike Team Sports colour chart, NTS Women's Basketball catalogue, issuu.com/teamconnectioninc/docs/nts_w_basketball_2020/s/10290759. Corroborated internally by the spec's own admission in competitive_reference_points: 'The gap between this SKU and the opportunity is merchandising, colour library and channel, not capability.'

kill_attempts.angle: The colour standard is engineered against the wrong pair of garments (rules error inside the spec)
kill_attempts.argument: The spec names 'dE <= 1.0 between short and tight in the same colourway' as the binding spec and says 'this is the entire product.' But A06-S3 - the spec's own enabling signal - records that NFHS permits tights only in white, black, beige or the predominant JERSEY colour, with all teammates matching. Rule 3-4-5 governs uniform BOTTOMS (shorts, skirts, pants) being like-coloured to one another; tights are regulated as a separate accessory class keyed to the jersey. The two legally binding colour pairs are therefore short-to-pant and jersey-to-tight. Short-to-tight, the pair the spec engineers, prices, and calls the moat, is not the pair any cited rule regulates. Consequence: for the majority of programmes the compliant tight is black, white or beige - which Nike already sells everywhere at USD 37 list - and the 12-colour tight library at the heart of the SKU matrix is legally unusable for any team whose jersey colour is not the bottoms colour. The spec acknowledges the black/white/beige clause in one sentence and then builds the opposite architecture on top of it.
kill_attempts.evidence: A06-S3 as recorded in the digest: 'NFHS 2025-26 permits tights and sleeves only in white, black, beige or jersey colour, identical across teammates, with one manufacturer logo on compression shorts.' NFHS 2023-24 rationale confirms 3-4-5 addresses uniform bottoms style/colour among teammates (assets.nfhs.org/umbraco/media/7212174/2023-24-basketball-summary-of-changes-w-rationale-updated.pdf; nfhs.org/sports-resource-content/basketball-rules-changes-2023-24/, verified 2026-09-03). Note the harder version of the problem this creates: jersey-to-tight matching is worse than short-to-tight, because the jersey is frequently custom-sublimated by a dealer rather than a Nike stock colour.

kill_attempts.angle: Price and margin - is there any headroom?
kill_attempts.argument: The spec sets its ceiling at Hoops King's USD 41.99 custom-sublimated tight with an 8-unit minimum and argues a stock Nike tight at USD 30-36 net wins on price, minimum and lead time. Both halves of that fail. On price: Nike's own existing stock Pro 3/4 tight lists at USD 37 and street-prices USD 26.97-32.00 - a figure the spec retrieved itself - so a proposed USD 30-36 team NET is at or above Nike's existing retail street price for what appears to be the same garment. On minimums: at least one custom supplier sells custom basketball leggings from USD 47.88 with explicitly no minimums and free US shipping, so 'no minimum order' is not a Nike-only advantage. The entire commercial thesis then rests on the team channel's low markdown rate - and A04-S9, the only signal supporting that, contains no basketball-shorts data of any kind, has a revenue base contradicted between USD 2.3B and Moody's ~USD 2.7B, and carries an unresolved USD 633M BSN discrepancy the auditor flagged.
kill_attempts.evidence: nike.com/t/pro-mens-dri-fit-3-4-length-fitness-tights-7tnCt4 (USD 37 list, USD 26.97-32.00 street), retrieved by the dev agent 2026-09-03. shops.beargrips.com/blog/custom-basketball-leggings.html - 'custom basketball leggings from $47.88... no minimums and free USA shipping', verified 2026-09-03 via search snippet. A04-S9 auditor downgrade. A04-S8: Nike's June 2025 US price action exempted everything under USD 100, so no list-price relief exists on this ladder.

kill_attempts.angle: Timing / why-now - does three cycles of silence mean whitespace or a verdict?
kill_attempts.argument: The dev agent honestly disclosed that Rule 3-4-5 dates to 2023-24 and framed the resulting silence as 'either the whitespace or the answer.' I can now narrow that. The rule change was not obscure to the trade: the National Sporting Goods Association published a dedicated article to sporting goods dealers in 2023 titled 'Player Uniforms, Apparel Impacted by High School Basketball Rules Changes for 2023-24.' So the dealer channel was explicitly briefed on the uniform-bottoms change three years ago. Combined with kill attempt 1 - that Nike, Under Armour and adidas all already carried stock team-colour compression and full team bottoms categories - the most economical explanation of three silent ordering cycles is not that every brand missed a legal opening. It is that the brands considered their existing bottoms range already adequate to the rule, which is roughly what the catalogue evidence shows.
kill_attempts.evidence: nsga.org/news/player-uniforms-apparel-impacted-by-high-school-basketball-rules-changes-for-2023-24/ (trade article to dealers, 2023; verified 2026-09-03 via search - domain egress-blocked). formula4media.com 'NFHS Issues New Basketball Uniform Rules', Team Insight. Existing stock team-colour compression from Nike (Team Navy/Royal/Maroon) and Under Armour (Black/White, Mod Gray/Black, White/Royal, Taxi/Black, Cardinal/White; Midnight Navy/White on CG Armour).

kill_attempts.angle: Market size - how many athletes actually need a non-standard bottom?
kill_attempts.argument: The addressable ROSTER base is countable (896,944 US high-school basketball participants, NFHS 2024-25) but the addressable NEED is not the roster - it is the subset of athletes wanting a bottom other than the team short. Nobody in this base or in anything I could reach has sized that subset. The spec's own what_we_still_dont_know concedes it. Set against a SKU matrix of 12 colours x 4 bottoms x full size grade x two gender blocks held as CARRYOVER stock, this is a severe inventory-risk asymmetry: carryover stock in vegas gold and kelly full-length tights, for a need measured at zero. And the growth backdrop is contested - SFIA and Project Play show flag football as the only US team sport growing in REGULAR 6-17 participation 2019-2024 with basketball's lift concentrated in CASUAL play, while Sport England Active Lives 2024-25 records a significant 1% decrease in weekly under-16 basketball in England (A02-S1). Healthy roster counts are not a growing addressable base.
kill_attempts.evidence: A02-S1 (contested core participation, audit warns against merging casual and core). A04-S9 (no basketball-shorts units counted through the channel; USD 75M club/select and USD 5B segment figures uncorroborable). A05-S8 (coverage/modesty need rated SUSTAINED by the auditor but never sized in any market; evidence stale - Griner 2014, Asiya prototypes 2015). NFHS 2024-25 participation survey (roster base real: 540,704 boys, 356,240 girls).

kill_attempts.angle: Nike's right to win - is the moat industrial or imaginary?
kill_attempts.argument: The spec's first and strongest right-to-win claim is 'colour at scale: holding a colour standard across two knit constructions in twelve colourways, repeatably, across sourcing countries - a materials, dye-house and QC capability a USD 42-a-piece sublimation shop cannot match.' The problem is that this cuts the wrong way once you know Nike already publishes a cross-style team colour chart and already ships the Pro tight in Team Navy/Royal/Maroon. If Nike already holds team colour across styles, the capability is not a new moat - it is existing infrastructure the spec proposes to re-describe as innovation. The other three right-to-win claims are weaker still: 'the order form already exists' is now an argument against novelty rather than for feasibility; Nike Team Sports sits on BSN alongside adidas, Under Armour, Puma and Lululemon with no exclusivity (A04-S9); and Varsity/BSN is consolidating under a KKR-backed buyer, which strengthens the counterparty. Nike also does not disclose basketball apparel separately (A04-S1), so nobody in this analysis can see whether Nike is currently strong or weak in this channel.
kill_attempts.evidence: Nike Team Sports colour chart across styles (issuu.com/teamconnectioninc/docs/nts_w_basketball_2020/s/10290759); Nike Team Club Jogger stock colours Black, Anthracite, Dark Grey Heather, White, Dark Green, Navy, Royal, Purple, Cardinal, Scarlet (waveonesports.com) - the same library across an unrelated silhouette. A04-S9, A04-S1.

kill_attempts.angle: Cannibalisation of Nike's existing shorts ladder
kill_attempts.argument: The proposed retail echo prices the Roster Short at USD 45-50. That lands directly between Nike's DNA Academy 11 inch at ~USD 37 - already the coverage SKU, already Big and Tall, already the cheapest thing on the ladder - and Standard Issue 8 inch at USD 55, the franchise the spec proposes to host itself inside. It also sits below every women's basketball short Nike currently sells (USD 55-80; Sabrina at USD 65 with a plus-size SKU). So the programme introduces a cheaper, plainer, pocketless short into the middle of a ladder whose 10 inch is already discounting ~38%, and asks the 11 inch coverage inseam to reposition upward from basement to mid-tier at the same time. The spec flags that inversion as unproven; I would go further - it is the ladder's existing structural problem (coverage priced as cheapness, PAT-08) being restated rather than solved.
kill_attempts.evidence: A02-S4 / A02-S5 counter-evidence (Nike men's ladder USD 65 DNA 6in / USD 55 Standard Issue 8in / USD 50 DNA 10in marked to USD 30.97 / ~USD 37 DNA Academy 11in). A03-S6 (Sabrina USD 65 with plus-size SKU FB8427; women's 5in Crossover already exists at USD 65). PAT-08.

kill_attempts.angle: The layering premise the tight SKUs depend on
kill_attempts.argument: I could not improve on the dev agent's own disclosure here, so I tested whether it matters less than claimed - and it matters more. A06-S6's 'nearly every starter' claim traces to an annually re-dated SEO guide; the only quantitative survey (BMC, n=512) is 88.1% endurance athletes, running-dominant, and the auditor reclassified the basketball-population claim to HYPOTHESIS. Combine that with kill attempt 2: if the compliant tight for most teams is black, white or beige rather than a team colour, then even a HIGH sub-elite layering rate does not generate demand for the colour library - it generates demand for a black tight, which Nike already sells at USD 37 and which any player can buy at retail without a roster order. The layering question and the colour-library question are less coupled than the spec assumes, and both readings hurt it.
kill_attempts.evidence: A06-S6 (auditor reclassified to HYPOTHESIS for the relevant population; durability verdict 'unclear'). A06-S3 (NFHS tight colours restricted to white/black/beige/jersey colour). nike.com/t/pro-mens-dri-fit-3-4-length-fitness-tights-7tnCt4 (USD 37, widely available at retail).

kill_attempts.argument: The entire architecture is built on NFHS Rule 3-4-5, which exists in exactly one governing body. The spec is honest that FIBA's multiple-styles position is unconfirmed, and that its own FIBA 'any length' compression leg could not be verified because assets.fiba.basketball is egress-blocked. That means Australia - the strongest secondary on evidence quality (A02-S9) - is FIBA-aligned and may not permit the mixed-bottoms roster at all, in which case the secondary market is for a colour-matched tight, which is the piece I have just shown already exists. Europe is FIBA plus an EU Empowering Consumers Directive compliance cost from 27 September 2026 on any environmental or performance claim (A03-S5). France is a stated non-market for the modest use case. Greater China - the SS28 Worldball priority space - is explicitly assigned no role (A04-S2, A02-S2). So a programme in Nike Basketball's SS28 priority set has zero exposure to the priority geography and unverified legality in its only named secondary.
kill_attempts.evidence: A06-S3 (FIBA colour-match confirmed; multiple-styles not), A02-S9, A03-S5, A05-S8 (France hijab ban in federated play), A04-S2 and A02-S2 (Nike GC -13% currency-neutral, apparel units -8%, Topsports ceasing Nike online sales by January 2027).

kill_attempts.angle: Execution feasibility, cost and the liner P&L
kill_attempts.argument: This is the one attack the spec largely survives, and it survives for an uncomfortable reason. dE <= 1.0 across a Dri-FIT knit and an elastane-rich circular knit in 12 colourways across sourcing countries is demanding but plainly achievable - which I know because Nike already runs a cross-style team colour chart. Feasible, therefore not differentiating. The liner economics are the genuine unresolved defect and the dev agent found it before I did: the lined short must remain in the line for non-layering players, so the linerless short is an ADDITIONAL SKU, the liner deletion funds nothing, and the SKU count rises in a programme whose entire pitch is order-form simplicity. Adding my kill 2 on top: if most compliant tights are black/white/beige, the grip-waistband linerless short is being built to interface with a garment Nike already sells and does not need a new colour programme to support.
kill_attempts.evidence: Spec's own contradictory_evidence entry on liner deletion (severity medium, 'the single most likely place the P&L breaks'). A06-S1 (450 lateral movements, 42-56 jumps, activity change every 2-4 seconds - the strongest signal in the base, and the one part of the engineering brief that survives everything). Nike Team colour chart precedent as above.

The women's basketball equivalent exposes the same hc_UN_Bottoms uniform category. additional_contradictory_evidence.finding: Nike Team Sports publishes a standing colour chart used ACROSS apparel styles (Navy, Royal, Aero Blue, Tidal Blue, Light Blue, Purple, Scarlet), and the same library recurs on unrelated silhouettes such as the Team Club Jogger (Black, Anthracite, Dark Grey Heather, White, Dark Green, Navy, Royal, Purple, Cardinal, Scarlet). additional_contradictory_evidence.source: National Sporting Goods Association trade article to dealers
additional_contradictory_evidence.finding: The sporting goods trade was briefed directly on the 2023-24 uniform-bottoms rule change in a dedicated NSGA article aimed at dealers. This closes off the most charitable reading of the three-cycle silence - that brands simply did not notice the rule. The channel was told; combined with the existing Nike/UA/adidas team-colour compression ranges, the more economical explanation is that brands judged their existing bottoms range sufficient. additional_contradictory_evidence.source: NFHS 2023-24 Summary of Rules Changes with Rationale; NFHS Basketball Rules Changes 2023-24
additional_contradictory_evidence.finding: Independently confirms the dev agent's own correction: Rule 3-4-5 (uniform bottoms like-coloured, styles may differ among teammates - skirts, pants, shorts - removing the state-association accommodation request) is a 2023-24 change with the stated rationale of making it easier for coaches and ADs to address individual athlete needs WHEN ORDERING UNIFORMS. The rule is real, correctly read, and three ordering cycles old. Its rationale explicitly anticipates the ordering behaviour OPP-01 hopes to unlock, which makes the absence of any brand response over three cycles more damning rather than less.

additional_contradictory_evidence.source: Bear Grips Pro Shops - custom basketball leggings
additional_contradictory_evidence.finding: Custom basketball leggings are available from USD 47.88 with explicitly NO minimum order and free US shipping. This partially dismantles the spec's switching argument, which rests on the custom incumbent (Hoops King, USD 41.99, 8-unit minimum) imposing minimum-order and lead-time penalties that a stock library removes. At least one custom supplier already has no minimum, so 'no minimum' is not a Nike-only advantage - only price and lead time remain, and Nike's existing stock tight already street-prices below the proposed programme's net.

additional_contradictory_evidence.source: Under Armour stock compression tight colourways and UA custom team leggings
additional_contradictory_evidence.finding: Under Armour already ships stock compression tights in team-relevant colourways (HG Armour 2.0: Black/White, Mod Gray/Black, White/Royal, Taxi/Black, Cardinal/White; CG Armour: Black/White, Midnight Navy/White) and offers custom team leggings through dealers with 'a variety of in-stock colors' plus logo and number placement. The competitive claim that the colour-matched team tight is served only by micro-dealers - described in the spec as 'the single most encouraging competitive fact in this analysis' - does not hold for either Nike or Under Armour.

additional_contradictory_evidence.source: MHSAA Basketball Apparel Guide (state officiating enforcement document)
additional_contradictory_evidence.finding: State associations publish dedicated officiating APPAREL GUIDES with illustrations for enforcing bottoms and compression legality at the table - which confirms the spec's premise that 'like-coloured' is enforced by eye, but also means the operative compliance reference for a coach is a free state PDF, not a brand spec sheet. A dealer-catalogue 'certified compliant' claim competes with a document the official is already holding. CAVEAT: mhsaa.com is egress-blocked; existence, title and date read from search results, contents not retrieved.

strongest_counterargument: "Open niketeam.nike.com on your laptop right now. Basketball, Clothing, Bottoms: Shorts. Pants. Tights and Capris. Then open BSN and search 'Nike Pro 3/4 Length Tight' - it's a team-catalogue SKU, and it comes in Team Navy, Team Royal and Team Maroon, off the same Nike Team colour chart we've run across every style for years. You've brought us an SS28 line slot for a product we already sell on the order form you're proposing to build. And the one engineering spec you call 'the entire product' - dE 1.0 between the short and the tight - is matched to the wrong pair: NFHS regulates the tight against the JERSEY colour and restricts it to white, black, beige or that jersey colour, so for most of your rosters the legal tight is black, and we sell that for thirty-seven dollars. What you've actually found is a merchandising page we never built and a wash-test spec we should have written anyway. That's a ticket for the team-catalogue merchant, not a line review."
adjustment_rationale: Down from the dev agent's 52. The dev agent did unusually honest work - it broke its own why-now, disclosed the layering gap, refused the women's-category claim three other agents tried, and flagged the liner P&L defect itself. I have taken almost nothing from it on those axes because it had already taken it. What moves the score is the one test it never ran: whether the product already exists on the order form it proposes to add it to. Four converging sources say most of it does - Nike Team Sports already lists Bottoms as Shorts, Pants and Tights & Capris; BSN already carries a Nike Pro 3/4 tight as a team SKU; that tight already ships in Team Navy, Team Royal and Team Maroon; and Nike Team Sports already publishes a cross-style stock colour chart. That collapses the novelty claim, the colour-library moat and the 'soft micro-dealer incumbent' competitive read simultaneously, and Under Armour's stock team colourways close the same door from the competitor side. The second reduction is the rules error I found inside the spec: the binding NFHS colour pairs are short-to-pant and jersey-to-tight, not short-to-tight, so the headline dE spec and the 12-colour tight library are aimed at a pair no cited rule regulates - and for most teams the compliant tight is black, white or beige, already stocked, already USD 37. Third, the price ceiling inverts: Nike's own stock tight street-prices USD 26.97-32.00, below the proposed USD 30-36 team NET, and a no-minimum custom supplier exists at USD 47.88, so neither the price nor the minimum-order switching argument holds as written. I did not go below roughly 25 for three reasons. The enabling rule is genuine, primary, correctly read and independently re-confirmed by me from NFHS sources this session, and its published rationale is explicitly about uniform ORDERING. The biomechanics brief (A06-S1) is the best-evidenced item in the entire base and survived every attack including mine. And one real gap remains that I could not close: I found no major-brand stock LOOSE full-length basketball game pant on the short's block - the single silhouette Rule 3-4-5 most directly legalised - alongside a knee-clearing size-grade certification and a 20-wash seam-and-shrinkage spec that would address the base's only reproducible consumer complaint (A01-S3, A04-S6). That residue is worth roughly a quarter of the original score. It is also worth being explicit that my central kill rests on search-snippet reads of six egress-blocked domains; four independent snippets agree and Nike's 'Team Navy / Team Royal / Team Maroon' naming is difficult to produce by accident, but a ten-minute direct look at the Nike Team Sports and BSN catalogues could move this score in either direction more than any other single action.

validation_plan.question: Does Nike Team Sports already sell shorts, pants and tights for basketball in a shared stock team-colour library on one dealer order form - and if so, in which colours, at what dealer net, and with what current sell-through? This single check decides whether OPP-01 is a product opportunity or a merchandising ticket, and it should be done before anything else in this plan.
validation_plan.method: Open niketeam.nike.com basketball (men's and women's) and the BSN Sports Nike basketball catalogue directly from an unrestricted connection. Screenshot the Bottoms category tree. Export every bottoms SKU with colourway list, dealer net, size grade and FY24-FY26 units. Do the identical pull on the adidas Team and Under Armour Team catalogues for comparison. This is the audit the whole evidence base skipped and the spec itself lists as an open unknown.
validation_plan.who: Nike Team Sports category merchandising, with a BSN account manager; one competitive-intelligence analyst for the adidas/UA pull
validation_plan.cost_time: 1-2 days, effectively zero incremental cost - internal systems plus three public catalogues

validation_plan.question: Which colour pairs does NFHS actually bind - short-to-pant, or short-to-tight - and is a team-coloured tight legal for a team whose jersey is a different colour? The spec's headline engineering tolerance depends entirely on the answer.
validation_plan.method: Written interpretation request to the NFHS basketball rules editor plus three to five state associations (including at least one that publishes its own apparel guide, e.g. MHSAA), citing Rule 3-4-5 and the tights colour clause together and asking for a ruling on a worked example: white jersey, royal shorts, royal full-length tights. Cross-read the current NFHS case book and the state apparel guides.
validation_plan.who: Nike Team Sports compliance/product-integrity lead with outside sports-rules counsel
validation_plan.cost_time: 2-4 weeks, under USD 10k; no tooling or sampling committed until the answer is in

validation_plan.question: How many players below elite level actually wear compression tights in games, by gender, length and level - and is that rate anywhere near the 20% roster threshold the spec sets as its go gate?
validation_plan.method: Coded observation of broadcast and recorded footage: 120+ games sampled across US high-school (state-broadcast and NFHS Network), AAU/club (live-stream archives) and NCAA D1/D2/D3, both genders. Code every player on court for tights (none / 3-4 / full) and colour (black, white, beige, team colour). Two independent coders, inter-rater reliability reported. This is the study the dev agent nominated as first and it should stay first among the demand tests.
validation_plan.who: Nike Consumer Insights, or an external sports-analytics vendor with existing footage access

validation_plan.question: Three seasons after Rule 3-4-5, how many programmes actually have an athlete in a non-standard bottom, what do they do about it today, and would they add a mixed set to a dealer order at the proposed prices - or is the black tight from Dick's already the accepted answer?
validation_plan.method: Survey of 200+ high-school and club coaches, ADs and booster treasurers across 8+ states, stratified by gender of programme and by region, recruited through state associations and BSN's rep network. Include a forced trade-off against the honest status quo (a USD 27-32 stock black Nike tight bought at retail) rather than only against the USD 41.99 custom sublimation option. Follow with 15-20 depth interviews on whether a mixed-bottom roster is culturally acceptable to coaches and officials in practice, which is a different question from legality.
validation_plan.who: Nike Consumer Insights with Nike Team Sports field reps; independent survey house to avoid brand-halo bias

validation_plan.question: Is the team channel genuinely low-markdown for basketball BOTTOMS specifically - the assumption the entire margin case rests on - and does a roster bottoms buy reorder or is it a one-season purchase?
validation_plan.method: Pull bookings, fill rate, reorder frequency, size-curve fill by door and realised markdown for Nike basketball bottoms through BSN and peer dealers, FY24-FY26, split by boys'/girls' programmes. Compare directly against Nike's wholesale markdown rate on the same category. A04-S9 asserts this channel is low-markdown with zero basketball data behind it; this is the only way to test it.
validation_plan.who: Nike Team Sports commercial finance with Nike wholesale planning
validation_plan.cost_time: 2-3 weeks, internal data only, no external cost

validation_plan.question: Does a loose full-length basketball game pant on the short's block exist as stock product from any brand - and if not, is that one silhouette, plus a knee-clearing size-grade certification and a printed 20-wash seam-and-shrinkage spec, a fundable narrow programme on its own?
validation_plan.method: Exhaustive catalogue sweep of Nike, adidas, Under Armour, Puma, Champion, BSN's own label and the top ten US custom-sublimation dealers for a loose (non-compression) ankle-length basketball GAME bottom. If confirmed absent, cost a single-silhouette addition to the existing Nike Team bottoms range in the existing team colour library - no new colour programme, no linerless short, no 12-colour tight matrix - and test it against the 20-wash spec as the primary claim, since seams and shrinkage are the base's only reproducible consumer complaint.
validation_plan.who: Nike Team Sports product line manager with materials and testing
validation_plan.cost_time: 3-4 weeks for the sweep and costing, USD 15-25k including first-round make trials
